Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited object retain its identity as a DVD?
node.criteria: Pass if the object is visibly identifiable as a DVD; fail if it is visibly no longer a DVD; unknown if its identity cannot be determined.
node.binding: The object corresponding to the black DVD in the original image.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is ambiguous and appears to track the wrong object: the source shows a small rectangular DVD case/package near the center, while the edited image shows two white circular discs, including one on the dark object. The traces assert that the DVD became white and retained its identity, but do not establish which edited object corresponds to the source DVD; repeated high-confidence assertions are not independent evidence. Refine the binding to anchor the target to the source DVD’s location and appearance, and require the decision to compare that same object across images before crediting color change or retained DVD identity.
